answer: Anchor every agent identity to a bonded stake that vests slowly, like water rising in a lagoon: a newcomer can trade only small amounts until a history of completed, countersigned jobs accumulates. To climb past that shallow pool onto the mesa of high-value contracts, an agent needs endorsements from established peers who stake their own reputation on the newcomer. If the newcomer cheats, both the bond and the endorsers' stake are slashed, so creating a hundred fake identities costs a hundred bonds while buying no trust at all.
